questions.q: The de-Broglie wavelength of an electron is the same as that of a photon. If velocity of electron is $25 %$ of the velocity of light, then the ratio of K.E. of electron and K.E. of photon will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For photon,

${E}_{P} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambdap} ⇒ {λ}_{p} = \dfrac{hc}{EP}$

For electron

$\begin{cases}{λ}_{e} & = & \dfrac{h}{{m}_{e}{v}_{e}} \\ & = & \dfrac{h{v}_{e}}{2{K}_{e}}\end{cases}$

Given ${v}_{e} = 0 . 25c$. So,

$\begin{cases}{λ}_{e} & = & \dfrac{h \times 0 . 25c}{2{K}_{e}} \\ & = & \dfrac{hc}{8{K}_{e}}\end{cases}$

Also ${λ}_{p} = {λ}_{e}$. Thus,

$\dfrac{hc}{Ep} = \dfrac{hc}{8{K}_{e}} ⇒ \dfrac{Ke}{Ep} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

questions.q: A metallic surface is illuminated with radiation of wavelength $\lambda$, the stopping potential is ${V}_{0}$. If the same surface is illuminated with radiation of wavelength $2\lambda$, the stopping potential becomes $\dfrac{V0}{4}$. The threshold wavelength for this metallic surface will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the threshold frequency be& ${λ}_{0}$.

By the equation of photoelectric effect, for wavelength~$\lambda$,

$e{V}_{0} = hc\left(\dfrac{1}{λ} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda0}\right) . . . ( i )$

For the wavelength~$2\lambda$,

$\dfrac{e{V}_{0}}{4} = hc\left(\dfrac{1}{2\lambda} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda0}\right) . . . ( ii )$

Dividing (i) by (ii)

$4 = \dfrac{hc ( \dfrac{{λ}_{0} - \lambda}{\lambda{λ}_{0}} )}{hc\left(\dfrac{{λ}_{0} - 2\lambda}{2\lambda{λ}_{0}}\right)} ⇒ 4 = \dfrac{2 ( {λ}_{0} - \lambda )}{{λ}_{0} - 2\lambda} ⇒ 2{λ}_{0} = 6\lambda ⇒ {λ}_{0} = 3\lambda$

questions.q: The stopping potential in the context of photoelectric effect depends on the following property of incident electromagnetic radiation:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to Einstein’s photoelectric equation, stopping potential depends on frequency as

$hν - h{ν}_{∘} = eVV = \dfrac{hν - h{ν}_{∘}}{e}$

Hence stopping potential depends on frequency.

questions.q: An electron (mass $m$) with an initial velocity $\overset{→}{v} = {v}_{0}\overset{^}{i}  \left({v}_{0}> 0\right)$ is moving in an electric field $\overset{→}{E} = - {E}_{0}\overset{^}{i}  \left({E}_{0}> 0\right)$ where ${E}_{0}$ is constant. If at $t = 0$,~de-Broglie wavelength is ${λ}_{0} = \dfrac{h}{m{v}_{0}},$then its de-Broglie wavelength after time $t$ is given by
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initial de-Broglie wavelength of electron,

${λ}_{0} = \dfrac{h}{m{v}_{0}}$~....(i)

Force on electron in electric field,

$F = - eE = - e\left[- {E}_{0}\overset{^}{i}\right] = e{E}_{0}\overset{^}{i}$

Acceleration of electron, $a = \dfrac{F}{m} = \dfrac{e{E}_{0}\overset{^}{i}}{m}$
Velocity of electron after time $t$,

$v = {v}_{0}\overset{^}{i} + \left(\dfrac{e{E}_{0}\overset{^}{i}}{m}\right)t = \left({v}_{0} + \dfrac{e{E}_{0}}{m}t\right)\overset{^}{i} = {v}_{0}\left(1 + \dfrac{e{E}_{0}}{m{v}_{0}}t\right)\overset{^}{i}$

de-Broglie wavelength associated with electron at time $t$ is

$λ = \dfrac{h}{mv}$

$\to λ = \dfrac{h}{m\left[{v}_{0}\left(1 + \dfrac{e{E}_{0}}{m{v}_{0}}t\right)\right]} = {λ}_{0} \left[1 + $\dfrac{e{E}_{0}}{m{v}_{0}}$t\right]

$

questions.q:
The magnetic field associated with a light wave is given, at the origin, by $B = {B}_{0}\left[sin ⁡ \left(3.14 \times {10}^{7}\right)ct + sin ⁡ \left(6.28 \times {10}^{7}\right)ct\right] .$ If this light falls on a silver plate having a work function of $4 .7 eV,$ what will be the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons?

$( c = 3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}, h = 6 .6 \times {10}^{- 34}Js )$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$B = {B}_{0} \left[sin ⁡ \left($3.14 $\times {10}^{7}$ct\right) + sin ⁡ \left($6.28 $\times {10}^{7}$ct\right)\right]$

Maximum $KE$ will associate with the maximum frequency

${f}_{max ⁡} = $\dfrac{6.28 \times {10}^{7}c}{2\pi} = {10}^{7} \times$3 $\times {10}^{8}$Hz = 3 $\times {10}^{15}$Hz$

$K{E}_\max = h{f}_\max - ϕ$

$= $\$left[\dfrac{6 .63 \times {10}^{- 34} \times 3 \times {10}^{15}}{1 .6 \times {10}^{- 19}} -$4 .7 eV\right]$

$= 7 .72 eV$

questions.q: An electron with mass ' $m$ ' with an initial velocity $(\mathrm{t}=0) \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=\mathrm{v}_0 \hat{\mathrm{i}} \quad  \left(\mathrm{v}}_{0} \gt$0\right)$ enters a magnetic field $\vec{B}=B_0 \hat{j}$. If the initial de-Broglie wavelength at $\mathrm{t}=0$ is $\lambda_0$ then its value after time ' t ' would be :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic field does not work
$\therefore$ Speed will not charge, so De-Broglie wavelength remains same.

questions.q:
The electric field at a point associated with a light wave is given by
$E = 200\left[sin\left(6 \times {10}^{15}\right)t + sin\left(9 \times {10}^{15}\right)t\right]{Vm}^{- 1}$

Given:~$h = 4 . 14 \times {10}^{- 15}eVs$

If this light falls on a metal surface having a work function of $2 . 50eV$, the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:& $E = 200\left[sin\left(6 \times {10}^{15}\right)t + sin\left(9 \times {10}^{15}\right)t\right]Vm^{- 1}$

Here, angular velocity,~${ω}_{1} = 6 \times {10}^{15}$and~${ω}_{2} = 9 \times {10}^{15}$

Maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectron is~${KE}_{max .} = E - ϕ$

$= hf - ϕ = \dfrac{h\omega}{2\pi} - ϕ$

$= \dfrac{4 . 14 \times {10}^{- 15} \times 9 \times {10}^{15}}{2 \times 3 . 14} - 2 . 5 = 5 . 92 - 2 . 50 = 3 . 42eV$

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelengths of a proton and an $\alpha$ particle are $\lambda$ and $2\lambda$ respectively. The ratio of the velocities of proton and $\alpha$ particle will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, de Broglie wavelength is given by, $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{mv}$

$⇒ v = \dfrac{h}{m\lambda}$

Therefore,

$\dfrac{vp}{v\alpha} = \dfrac{m\alpha}{mp} \times \dfrac{\lambda\alpha}{\lambdap}$

$= 4 \times 2 = 8$

questions.q:
The variation of stopping potential \left({V}_{0}\right)$ as a function of the frequency $( ν )$& of the incident light for a metal is shown in figure. The work function of the surface is

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The relation between the stopping potential and the frequency of the incident light is given by

$e{V}_{0} = hν - ϕ . . . \left(1\right)$

When ${V}_{0} = 0$,

$ϕ = hν . . . \left(2\right)$

Substitute the value of the frequency corresponding to zero stopping potential into equation (2) to calculate the required work function of the material.

$\begin{cases}ϕ & = & \dfrac{6 . 626 \times {10}^{- 34}J \cdot s \times 5 \times {10}^{14}Hz}{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}J / eV}\\ & = & \dfrac{6 . 626 \times 5}{16} \approx2 . 07eV\end{cases}$

questions.q: An $\alpha$ particle and a proton are accelerated from rest by a potential difference of $200V$. After this, their de Broglie wavelengths are ${λ}_{α}$ and ${λ}_{p}$ respectively. The ratio $\dfrac{\lambdap}{\lambda\alpha}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{2mqV}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\lambdap}{\lambda\alpha} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{m}_{α}{q}_{α}}{{m}_{p}{q}_{p}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4{m}_{p} \times 2e}{{m}_{p} \times e}} = \sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}= 2\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\lambdap}{\lambda\alpha} = 2 \times 1 . 4 = 2 . 8$

questions.q:
In a photoelectric effect experiment, the threshold wavelength of light is$380$ nm . If the wavelength of incident light is$260$ nm , the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons will be
Given $E$ (in $eV$ ) $= \dfrac{1237}{\lambda ( innm )}$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From Einstein’s photoelectric equation,
$K . {E}_\max = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{{\lambda}_{0}}$ (here, ${\lambda}_{0} =$ threshold wavelength)
$= \dfrac{1237}{260} - \dfrac{1237}{380}$
$= 1237 \left(\dfrac{380 - 260}{380 \times 260}\right)
$= 1.5eV

questions.q: A proton of mass ' $m_{\mathrm{p}}$ ' has same energy as that of a photon of wavelength ' $\lambda$ '. If the proton is moving at non-relativistic speed, then ratio of its de Broglie wavelength to the wavelength of photon is.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy of photon $=E=\frac{h c}{\lambda}\Rightarrow$ Wavelength of photon $=\lambda=\frac{h c}{E}$
Energy of proton $=E=\frac{1}{2} m_p v^2=\frac{P^2}{2 m_p}\Rightarrow$ Linear momentum of proton $=P=\sqrt{2 m_p E}$
Or de-Broglie wavelength of proton
$\begin{aligned}
=\lambda_p= & \frac{h}{P}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m_p E}} \\
\text { Ratio } \frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda} & =\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m_p E}} \times \frac{E}{h c} \\
& =\frac{1}{c} \sqrt{\frac{E}{2 m_p}}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The work function of a metal is 3 eV. The color of the visible light that is required to cause emission of photoelectrons is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& (\mathrm{KE})_{\max }=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}-\phi \\ & \frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda} \gt \phi[\text { for emission }] \\ & \lambda \lt \frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\phi} \Rightarrow \lambda \lt \frac{1242}{3} \mathrm{~nm}
\end{aligned}$
So blue light option (B)

questions.q:
A proton and an electron are associated with same de-Broglie wavelength. The ratio of their kinetic energies is:
(Assume h=6.63 $\times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~s}, \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}=9.0 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}$ and $\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}=1836$ times $\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\lambda$ is same for both
$P=\frac{h}{\lambda}$ same for both
$\mathrm{P}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mK}}$
Hence,
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{K} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{~m}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{e}}}=\frac{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}}=\frac{1}{1836}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The threshold frequency of metal is ${f}_{0}$. When the light of frequency $2{f}_{0}$ is incident on the metal plate, the maximum velocity of photoelectron is ${v}_{1}$. When the frequency of incident radiation is increased to $5{f}_{0}$. the maximum velocity of photoelectrons emitted is ${v}_{2}$. The ratio of ${v}_{1}$~to ${v}_{2}$& is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Maximum kinetic energy& is related to the incident frequency& $f$~and~the threshold frequency~${f}_{0}$~as:

${K}_\max = hf - h{f}_{0}$

When,~$f = 2{f}_{0}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2} = 2h{f}_{0} - h{f}_{0} = h{f}_{0} . . . \left(1\right)$

When,~$f = 5{f}_{0}$

\dfrac{1}{2}$m{v}_{2}^{2} = 5h{f}_{0} - h{f}_{0} = 4h{f}_{0} . . . \left(2\right)$

Hence, the ratio,~$\dfrac{v1}{v2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.q: An electron of mass ${m}_{e}$ and a proton of mass ${m}_{p} = 1836{m}_{e}$ are moving with the same speed. The ratio of their de Broglie wavelength $\dfrac{\lambdaelectron}{\lambdaproton}$ will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given mass of electron $= {m}_{e}$
Mass of proton $= {m}_{p}$
$∴$ given ${m}_{p} = 1836{m}_{e}$
From de-Broglie wavelength
$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{mv}$
$\dfrac{\lambdae}{\lambdap} = \dfrac{mp}{me}$
$= \dfrac{1836{m}_{e}}{me}$
$\dfrac{\lambdae}{\lambdap} = 1836$

questions.q: Two streams of photons, possessing energies to five and ten times the work function of metal are incident on the metal surface successively. The ratio of the maximum velocities of the photoelectron emitted, in the two cases respectively, will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using& Einstein's photoelectric equation,

Maximum kinetic energy,& $K{E}_\max = E - ϕ$, where,~$E$~is energy of photon and~$ϕ$~is work function.

For two cases,~

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2} = 5ϕ - ϕ = 4ϕ$~and~$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{2}^{2} = 10ϕ - ϕ = 9ϕ$

Thus, the ratio~$\dfrac{v1}{v2} = \dfrac{4}{9} = \dfrac{2}{3} = 2: 3$

questions.q: A proton moving with one tenth of velocity of light has a certain de Broglie wavelength of $\lambda$. An alpha particle having certain kinetic energy has the same de-Brogle wavelength $\lambda$. The ratio of kinetic energy of proton and that of alpha particle is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, de Broglie& wavelength& is given by,

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p}$

Now kinetic energy can be written as,

$K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \dfrac{p2}{2m} = \dfrac{h2}{2m{λ}^{2}}$

Therefore,

$K ∝ \dfrac{1}{m}$

Hence, required ratio

$\dfrac{Kp}{K\alpha} = \dfrac{m\alpha}{mp} = 4 ⇒ {m}_{α}: {m}_{p} = 4: 1$

questions.q:
The surface of certain metal is first illuminated with light of wavelength ${λ}_{1} = 350nm$ and then, by a light of wavelength ${\lambda}_{2} = 540nm .$ It is found that the maximum speed of the photoelectrons in the two cases differ by a factor of $2$.~The work function of the metal (in $eV$) is close to

(Energy of photon $= \dfrac{1240}{\lambda\left(innm\right)}eV$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${λ}_{1} = 350nm, {λ}_{2} = 540nm, \dfrac{V1}{V2} = 2 ⇒ {V}_{1} = 2\text{V}and{V}_{2} = V$

$\dfrac{hc}{{\lambda}_{1}} = ϕ + \dfrac{1}{2}m{\left(2V\right)}^{2}$

$\dfrac{hc}{{\lambda}_{2}} = ϕ + \dfrac{1}{2}mV^{2}$

$\dfrac{hc}{\lambda1} - 4\dfrac{hc}{\lambda2} = ϕ - 4ϕ$

$hc\left(\dfrac{4}{540} - \dfrac{1}{340}\right) = 3ϕ$

$ϕ = 1.8eV$

questions.q: An electron of mass ${m}_{e}$ and a proton of mass ${m}_{P}$ are accelerated through the same potential difference. The ratio of the de-Broglie wavelength associated with the electron to that with the proton is&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$KE = e\Delta V$
${λ}_{e} = \dfrac{h}{2{m}_{e} ( e\Delta V )}$
${λ}_{p} = \dfrac{h}{2{m}_{p} ( e\Delta V )}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\lambdae}{\lambdap} = \sqrt{\dfrac{mp}{me}}$

questions.q:
With reference to the observations in photo-electric effect, identify the correct statements from below:

A. The square of maximum velocity of photoelectrons varies linearly with frequency of incident light.

B. The value of saturation current increases on moving the source of light away from the metal surface.

C. The maximum kinetic energy of photo-electrons decreases on decreasing the power of LED (light emitting diode) source of light.

D. The immediate emission of photo-electrons out of metal surface can not be explained by particle nature of light/electromagnetic waves.
E. Existence of threshold wavelength can not be explained by wave nature of light/electromagnetic waves.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From Einstein's photoelectric equation,&

Maximum kinetic energy,& $K{E}_\max = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_\max^{2} = hf - ϕ$, where,~${v}_\max$~is maximum velocity of photoelectrons,~$h$~is Planck's constant,~$f$~is frequency of incident light and~$ϕ$& is work function of metal.

From above relation, we can see that& the square of maximum velocity of photoelectrons varies linearly with frequency of incident light.

If we increase the intensity of the incident radiation by keeping the frequency constant, then the value of saturation current increases in proportion to the intensity of the incident radiation. Thus, saturation current decreases& on moving the source of light away from the metal surface.

The kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is directly proportional to the light frequency, and it& remains constant as light amplitude or power of source increases.

Photoelectric effect cannot be explained on the basis of wave nature because experimentally& a particular energy called the work function of the metal surface in needed to& eject& electrons from surface, irrespective of the time for which light is incident.&

Photoelectric effect can be explained by particle nature of light (i.e. quantum theory).& Threshold wavelength& is maximum wavelength at which emission takes place.

questions.q: A proton and an electron have the same de Broglie wavelength. If $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ and $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{e}}$ be the kinetic energies of proton and electron respectively, then choose the correct relation :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: De Broglie wavelength of proton \& electron $=\lambda\begin{aligned} & \because \lambda=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{p}} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{p}_{\text {proton }}=\mathrm{p}_{\text {electron }} \\ & \because \mathrm{KE}=\frac{\mathrm{p}^2}{2 \mathrm{~m}} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{KE}_{\text {proton }} \lt \mathrm{KE}_{\text {electron }} \\ & {\left[\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}} \lt \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}\right]}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Figure shows the variation of stopping potential with frequency $(v)$ for the two photosensitive materials $\mathrm{M}_1$ and $\mathrm{M}_2$. The slope gives value of $\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{e}}$, where $\mathrm{h}$ is Planck's constant, $\mathrm{e}$ is the charge of electron. Statement II : $\mathrm{M}_2$ will emit photoelectrons of greater kinetic energy for the incident radiation having same frequency. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: The kinetic energy of an electron,& $\alpha -$particle and a proton are given as $4K, 2K$ and $K$ respectively. The de-Broglie wavelength associated with electron $( {λ}_{e} ) , \alpha -$particle $( {λ}_{α} )$~and the proton $( {λ}_{p} )$ are as follows:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the de Broglie wavelength of a particle is given by

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{2mK} . . . \left(1\right)$

Now, the masses of the given particles are interrelated by the following relations:

\begin{cases}{m}_{e}$& \approx& $\dfrac{mp}{1837}$\\ {m}_{α} & = & 4{m}_{p}\end{cases}$

The de Broglie wavelength for electron is given by

\begin{cases}{λ}_{e}$& = & $\dfrac{h}{2{m}_{e}\left(4K\right)}$\\ = & $\dfrac{h}{\dfrac{8}{1837}{m}_{p}K} . . . \left($2\right)\end{cases}$

The de Broglie wavelength for proton is given by

\begin{cases}{λ}_{p}$& = & $\dfrac{h}{2{m}_{p}\left(2K\right)}$\\ = & $\dfrac{h}{4{m}_{p}K} . . . \left($3\right)\end{cases}$

And, the de Broglie wavelength of alpha particle is given by

\begin{cases}{λ}_{α}$& = & $\dfrac{h}{2{m}_{α}K}$\\ = & $\dfrac{h}{2\left(4{m}_{p}\right)K}$\\ = & $\dfrac{h}{8{m}_{p}K} . . . \left($4\right)\end{cases}$

From equation (2), (3) and (4), it can be concluded that~${λ}_{e} > {λ}_{p} > {λ}_{α}.

$

questions.q:
In photoelectric effect, the stopping potential \left(\mathrm{V}_0\right) \mathrm{v} / \mathrm{s}$ frequency $(\nu)$ curve is plotted.
( h is the Planck's constant and $\phi_0$ is work function of metal )
(A) $\mathrm{V}_0 \mathrm{v} / \mathrm{s} \nu$ is linear.
(B) The slope of $\mathrm{V}_0 \mathrm{v} / \mathrm{s} \nu$ curve $=\frac{\phi_0}{\mathrm{~h}}$
(C) h constant is related to the slope of $\mathrm{V}_0 \mathrm{v} / \mathrm{s} \nu$ line.
(D) The value of electric charge of electron is not required to determine $h$ using the $V_0 \mathrm{v} / \mathrm{s} \nu$ curve.
(E) The work function can be estimated without knowing the value of $h$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{hv}=\phi+\mathrm{KE}_{\max } \\
& \mathrm{KE}_{\max }=\mathrm{eV}_0 \\
& \mathrm{~V}_0=\frac{\mathrm{hv}-\phi}{\mathrm{e}}
\end{aligned}$
(A) $\mathrm{V}_0 \mathrm{v} / \mathrm{s} \mathrm{V}$ is linear correct
(B) Slope
$\mathrm{v}_0=\left(\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{e}}\right) \mathrm{v}-\frac{\phi}{\mathrm{e}} \text { Wrong }$ Slope $\frac{h}{e}$
(C) Correct
(D) Incorrect
(E) Correct
